## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sumanātherīgāthā* (Thig 1.14) is a short verse text located within the *Therīgāthā*, a collection of poems by enlightened Buddhist elder nuns in the *Khuddakanikāya* of the Pali Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text represents the poetic utterance attributed to the elder nun (therī) Sumanā [SuttaCentral]. While modern research tools index the poem widely, listing thirteen translations across ten modern languages including English translations by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato, none of the secondary literature passages in the present dossier address this poem, dealing instead with various other historical, mythical, or lexical homonyms of the name Sumana [SuttaCentral].

In terms of parallels and textual reuse, SuttaCentral records no curated parallels in the Chinese Āgamas, Tibetan Kangyur, or elsewhere in early Buddhist literature [SuttaCentral]. In agreement with this, automated analysis by DharmaNexus found no Pali-internal text reuse and no cross-language matches with a significant similarity score in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus].
